items.title: Earl May interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2001
items.q: So Bob is trying to work on that for me.

ctx.x: There’s a reason you’re doing that. That’s a good one. How’s the musician’s union been for you over the years?

It’s been kind of dormant really. But we have people in there like Bob Cranshaw and Jimmy Owens and people that are really and -- And at one time Benny Powell was in there really pushing them really to help, to bring jazz musicians up to par. So it looks, because I did a lot of things, I was in the Playboy Club for instance once for a while, playing with Kai Winding, then I had my own quartet there or a while. Because I just wanted to stay around town. It was a good place, to have a nice, steady jazz gig and you…
Yeah. It’s unfortunate that so many musicians don’t end up with what they should. Does the music tend to keep you young do you think?
